identity.name: Banu Qasi
alt_names: Banu Qasi lords of the Ebro

land.text: Zaragoza and Tudela, entered by the sons of Musa ibn Musa in 872

predecessors.note: The family held offices for the emirs from 788 (Musa ibn Furtun suppressing a revolt in Zaragoza for Hisham I) and Musa ibn Musa was named Wali of Zaragoza in 851/852 after a victory at Albelda; the dossier starts when they took Zaragoza and Tudela in 872.

land.text: Nájera and Viguera in La Rioja

successors.note: 924: Abd ar-Rahman III's punitive campaign removes the Banu Qasi from Tudela; the Tujibids take their place.

capitals.name: Zaragoza
capitals.note: 'Isma'il ibn Musa enters Zaragoza' in 872; the page names no capital.

capitals.name: Tudela
capitals.note: The family's seat after the emir took Zaragoza in 884 and gave it to the Tujibids in 886; 'Furtun occupies Tudela' in 872.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 872-883. Cliopatria has no Banu Qasi row. The page: 'Isma'il ibn Musa enters Zaragoza' and 'Furtun occupies Tudela' in 872, after the rebellion in Huesca of 870 'that would bring the Banu Qasi back to dominance'; Albelda in La Rioja was Musa ibn Musa's fortress in 859 (Ordoño I page) but the page gives no boundary, so Zaragoza province and Tudela are the readings. [Repair eu-12-a: Monzón added ('the two of them together taking Monzon', January 872).]
New keyframe, 884-897: 'In 884 the emir sent two military campaigns into the region and took Zaragoza'; in 886 the new emir gave it to the rival Tujibids. Tudela stays.
New keyframe, 898-913: Lubb ibn Muhammad 'recognizes Emir Abd Allah in exchange for the governorship of Tudela and Tarazona'.

union.text: Nájera and Viguera in La Rioja

correction.text: Tudela and Tarazona, Monzón and Lleida, Nájera and Viguera

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 914-922: 'Muhammad ibn Lubb regains Monzon and Lleida' (914); in 918 Ordoño II and Sancho I 'ravage Banu Qasi lands around Viguera, Nájera, and Tudela', so the Rioja lands are theirs by 918 (the page does not say when they were acquired: conf 1 in the ledger). In 914 Sancho takes Arnedo.

correction.text: Tudela and Tarazona, Monzón and Lleida

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 923: 'Viguera and Nájera fall' (the Banu Qasi page); Muhammad ibn Abd Allah is captured and assassinated.

New keyframe, 924-928: 'Abd ar-Rahman III's punitive campaign removes the Banu Qasi from Tudela' (924); in 928 Muhammad ibn Lubb 'holds only Ayera, after Jimeno Garcés intervenes on his behalf'. Ayera is read as Ayerbe (Huesca) (conf 1); what became of Monzón and Lleida is not on the page.

ledger.note: 872: the sons of Musa ibn Musa take Zaragoza and Tudela. 'Isma'il ibn Musa enters Zaragoza, and Lubb joins him. Furtun occupies Tudela.' The land is the province of Zaragoza and Tudela. 'In January 872, Isma'il ibn Musa entered Zaragoza, and was there joined by Lubb, the two of them together taking Monzon.' [Repair eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: Monzón added to the land, to agree with the emirate's January 872 loss.]
884: the emir takes Zaragoza. 'In 884 the emir sent two military campaigns into the region and took Zaragoza'; the next emir gave it to the Tujibids in 886.

By 884 Monzón is no longer Banu Qasi land: the page has Muhammad ibn Lubb 'regain' Monzón and Lleida in 914, so it was lost, but it does not say when or to whom. Entered at 884, the year the emir took Zaragoza, to bridge the silence (confidence 1); keyframe 884-897 draws Tudela only. [Repair eu-12-a, 2026-10-25]

898: the Banu Qasi hold Tudela and Tarazona as the emir's vassals. Lubb ibn Muhammad 'formally recognized the sovereignty of the emir, Abd Allah, in exchange for the formal governorship' of the two towns; the mirror of emirate-of-cordoba's vassal_start of 898, which lasts until 924.

898: Lubb ibn Muhammad is given Tarazona, with Tudela already his. He 'recognizes Emir Abd Allah in exchange for the governorship of Tudela and Tarazona' after his father Muhammad ibn Lubb was killed at Zaragoza on 8 October. [Repair eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: the gain is Tarazona only (Tudela was Banu Qasi land from 872); the vassalage over both is the next event.]
914: Muhammad ibn Lubb regains Monzón and Lleida. 'Muhammad ibn Lubb regains Monzon and Lleida'; the page does not say from whom they were taken.

region.text: Nájera and Viguera in La Rioja

ledger.note: 914: the Rioja lands around Nájera and Viguera are in Banu Qasi hands. The page has Sancho taking Arnedo and attacking Calahorra in 914 and 'Banu Qasi lands around Viguera, Nájera, and Tudela' in 918; it does not date their acquisition.
914: Sancho Garcés takes Arnedo. 'Sancho takes Arnedo and attacks Calahorra.'

region.text: Nájera and Viguera in La Rioja

ledger.note: 923: Viguera and Nájera fall. 'Viguera and Nájera fall. Muhammad ibn Abd Allah is captured and assassinated.' The Navarre page gives Sancho Garcés 'the regions of Nájera and Calahorra'.

924: Abd al-Rahman III ends the vassalage by removing the Banu Qasi from Tudela: 'on his return to Tudela he removed the Banu Qasi and sent them to Córdoba'. The mirror of emirate-of-cordoba's vassal_end of 924; the land passes to the Tujibids in the next event.

924: Abd al-Rahman III removes the Banu Qasi from Tudela. the Banu Qasi page: 'on his return to Tudela he removed the Banu Qasi and sent them to Córdoba', the year after 'Viguera and Najera fell' (923); the Tujibids take their place. [Reviewer eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: source changed from the Abd al-Rahman III page, which does not name Tudela.]
929: the Banu Qasi end in the Ebro valley. 'The death of Muhammad ibn Lubb marked the end of the Banu Qasi in the Ebro valley.'

wars.name: Banu Qasi revolts against Córdoba
wars.outcome: Musa ibn Musa revolts with Íñigo Arista in the 840s and is defeated by Abd ar-Rahman II (his son Lubb taken hostage); after the 870 Huesca rebellion the family returns to dominance (872), Mutarrif and his sons are crucified at Córdoba in 873 and the emir takes Zaragoza in 884.
wars.note: [Reviewer eu-12-x, 2026-10-25: from moved 840 -> 872, the state's start, so the war lies inside the life; the family revolts began in the 840s, before the 872 state]

wars.name: Wars of Sancho Garcés I and Abd al-Rahman III against the Banu Qasi

union.text: Nájera and Viguera in La Rioja

zones.text: Tudela, Nájera, Viguera, Monzón and Lleida

wars.outcome: Lubb is killed at Liédena (30 September 907); Sancho takes Arnedo (914) and captures Abd Allah at Tudela (915); Ordoño II and Sancho ravage Viguera, Nájera and Tudela (918); Viguera and Nájera fall (923); the emir removes them from Tudela (924); Muhammad ibn Lubb holds only Ayera (928) and dies in 929.
wars.note: The page has two men called Muhammad ibn Lubb (killed at Zaragoza in 898; alive in 914 and 928-929); the dossier does not list rulers because the page does not settle the sequence.

certainty.note: Held towns and fortresses along the Ebro; the page gives no boundary lines.

sources.title: Banu Qasi
sources.note: The dated career of the family 788-929: Zaragoza, Tudela, Tarazona, Monzón, Lleida, Nájera, Viguera, Ayera.

sources.title: Ordoño I of Asturias
sources.note: Musa ibn Musa's fortress of Albelda; the battle of Monte Laturce.

notes: A direct counterpart of the Emirate of Córdoba, Pamplona and Asturias that no Cliopatria row covers, written from one page (Banu Qasi) plus the Ordoño I and Abd al-Rahman III pages already opened. Start 872 (the sons take Zaragoza and Tudela) although the family governed for the emirs from 788 and Musa ibn Musa was Wali of Zaragoza from 851/852; the 840s revolt and 859 defeat precede it. The Tujibids (Zaragoza from 886, Tudela from 924) and Muhammad al-Tawil of Huesca (907 Ribagorza, 911) are not written; they need dossiers or a place in the taifa-of-zaragoza dossier. Rulers are omitted: the page names two men Muhammad ibn Lubb. Ayera is read as Ayerbe; every region is a reading of towns (conf 2 or 1). Names needed in the gazetteer: Tudela, Tarazona, Monzón, Lleida (place), Nájera, Viguera, Arnedo, Albelda, Ayerbe. Repair 2026-10-25 (eu-12-a, after the review of emirate-of-cordoba): Monzón is Banu Qasi land from January 872 (the page: 'the two of them together taking Monzon'), lost by 884 at confidence 1 (the page's 'regains' in 914 shows only that it was lost); the 898 submission is now a vassal_start/vassal_end pair with emirate-of-cordoba (898-924), the gain being Tarazona only. Not touched: the 924 loss of Monzón, Lleida and Ayerbe (keyframe 924 still draws Ayerbe only) and the Rioja dates, left as the reviewer's gaps.
